item.title: The Drug That Put a Brake on Lung Decline — Rapa Nui Rapamycin (Sirolimus), FKBP12–FRB Ternary Complex (PDB 1FAP), TSC2 Loss in Lymphangioleiomyomatosis (MILES Trial) & Whole-Blood LC–MS/MS vs. Immunoassay TDM
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 88: Rapa Nui Rapamycin (Sirolimus), FKBP12–FRB Ternary Complex (PDB 1FAP), TSC2 Loss in Lymphangioleiomyomatosis (MILES Trial) & Whole-Blood LC–MS/MS vs. Immunoassay TDM. A woman pauses on the landing. Her latest forced breath confirms what the stairs have been telling her for a year. The Critical Care Clinician measures the loss of airflow; the Molecular Pharmacologist follows a microbial molecule that brings two human proteins together. The patient, clinical measurements and host exchanges are fictional. The notebook anchor is section 1.4.1, “Sirolimus (Rapamycin),” of Michael C. Milone’s 2016 chapter “Overview of the pharmacology and toxicology of immunosuppressant agents that require therapeutic drug monitoring.” Pharmacology notebook · Chapter record

item.title: The Days After the Bleed — Delayed Cerebral Ischemia After Aneurysmal SAH, Dihydropyridine Cav1.2 Fenestration Binding (PDB 5KMF / 8HMB), Pickard British Aneurysm Nimodipine Trial & Wrong-Route IV Boxed Warning
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 89: Delayed Cerebral Ischemia After Aneurysmal SAH, Dihydropyridine Cav1.2 Fenestration Binding (PDB 5KMF / 8HMB), Pickard British Aneurysm Nimodipine Trial & Wrong-Route IV Boxed Warning. Six days after a ruptured aneurysm is secured, a woman who was speaking clearly can no longer name a key. The Critical Care Clinician follows her exam, arterial pressure and cerebral circulation. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows nimodipine from a Bayer patent into a membrane pocket, then asks which human outcomes changed. The case, values and dialogue are fictional. The Pharmacology notebook chapter “Voltage-Gated Calcium Channel Antagonists for the Central Nervous System” (2010) provides channel taxonomy through its Table 1 entry for CaV1.2/α1C. Primary studies supply the nimodipine evidence. Pharmacology notebook

item.title: The Memory Drug and the Missing Beat — Donepezil Dual-Site Human AChE Gorge Spanning, Rogers & AD2000 Dementia Trials, Cholinergic Sinoatrial/AV Nodal Syncope & Prescribing-Cascade Pacemaker Risk
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 90: Donepezil Dual-Site Human AChE Gorge Spanning, Rogers & AD2000 Dementia Trials, Cholinergic Sinoatrial/AV Nodal Syncope & Prescribing-Cascade Pacemaker Risk. A woman taking donepezil briefly loses consciousness while seated. Later, while she is still on the monitor, the feeling returns. The Critical Care Clinician follows the atrial impulses that fail to reach her ventricles. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows Eisai’s inhibitor from the acetylcholinesterase gorge to the cognitive trials and the cardiac safety data. The patient, timings, bedside measurements and host dialogue are fictional. The notebook anchor is Brett A. English and Andrew A. Webster’s 2012 chapter 132, Acetylcholinesterase and its Inhibitors, which discusses donepezil’s reversible inhibition and Alzheimer indication. Pharmacology notebook · English and Webster chapter

item.title: The Patch That Changed a Pain Fiber — Caterina's 1997 TRPV1 Cloning, Vanilloid Pocket Cryo-EM (PDB 7LPE), Reversible Epidermal Nerve-Fiber Defunctionalization (Kennedy) & 8% Capsaicin Patch Trials
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 85: Caterina's 1997 TRPV1 Cloning, Vanilloid Pocket Cryo-EM (PDB 7LPE), Reversible Epidermal Nerve-Fiber Defunctionalization (Kennedy) & 8% Capsaicin Patch Trials. A sock hurts a woman’s feet. A concentrated patch activates the channel that makes chili feel hot, yet her pain diary later records less burning. The patient, measurements and dialogue are fictional. The notebook anchor is Roman V. Frolov and Matti Weckström’s chapter “Harnessing the Flow of Excitation: TRP, Voltage-Gated Na⁺, and Voltage-Gated Ca²⁺ Channels in Contemporary Medicine,” published online December 10, 2015 and in the 2016 volume. Chapter record Pharmacology notebook

item.title: The Drug That Kept GABA Outside — Tiagabine Off-Label Nonconvulsive Status Epilepticus, Human GAT1 Inward-Occluded Cryo-EM (PDB 7SK2 / 7Y7Z), Extrasynaptic Tonic GABAA & Salzburg EEG Criteria
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 86: Tiagabine Off-Label Nonconvulsive Status Epilepticus, Human GAT1 Inward-Occluded Cryo-EM (PDB 7SK2 / 7Y7Z), Extrasynaptic Tonic GABAA & Salzburg EEG Criteria. A woman with no known epilepsy stops answering questions halfway through a sentence. A new medication was meant to help her anxiety. The Critical Care Clinician follows her examination and video-EEG while the Molecular Pharmacologist tracks the GABA that remains outside neurons and astrocytes after GAT1 inhibition. The patient, measurements and dialogue are fictional. The notebook anchor, “Pharmacology and Biochemistry of Synaptic Transmission: Classical Transmitters,” is chapter 7 of the third edition of From Molecules to Networks (2014). It introduces high-affinity GABA uptake. The drug-specific evidence comes from the original studies and records linked below. Pharmacology notebook

item.title: The Blood Pressure Drug That Reached the Classroom — Guanfacine from Centrally Acting Antihypertensive to Prefrontal Alpha-2A HCN Regulation, Cryo-EM (PDB 7EJ8) & Pediatric ADHD/Tic RCTs
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 87: Guanfacine from Centrally Acting Antihypertensive to Prefrontal Alpha-2A HCN Regulation, Cryo-EM (PDB 7EJ8) & Pediatric ADHD/Tic RCTs. An 11-year-old wants to finish the first problem on a worksheet before losing their place. Their parent asks whether the same medicine might help the shoulder jerks and throat sounds that interrupt reading aloud. The Critical Care Clinician follows symptoms, daily function and circulation. The Molecular Pharmacologist traces an antihypertensive patent through receptor assays, primate recordings and trials with different clinical endpoints. The patient, observations and host dialogue are fictional. The notebook anchor is Andreas Hartmann’s 2013 chapter Clinical Pharmacology of Nondopaminergic Drugs in Tourette Syndrome, section 2.2 on guanfacine. Pharmacology notebook · Hartmann chapter

item.title: The Signal That Stopped the Migraine — Humphrey's 5-HT1B/1D Vascular Hypothesis, Subcutaneous Sumatriptan (US4816470 / US5037845), 5-HT1B Cryo-EM Comparator (PDB 6G79) & Human PET/MRA
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 83: Humphrey's 5-HT1B/1D Vascular Hypothesis, Subcutaneous Sumatriptan (US4816470 / US5037845), 5-HT1B Cryo-EM Comparator (PDB 6G79) & Human PET/MRA. A woman recognizes her usual migraine, but vomiting has made it difficult to keep fluids and tablets down. The Critical Care Clinician checks the time course, neurologic examination and vascular history. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows Glaxo’s GR43175 from vascular experiments and patent claims to human receptor pharmacology. The patient, observations and dialogue are fictional. The notebook source is Bockaert and colleagues’ 2010 chapter on serotonin receptor classification and signaling, specifically its discussion of 5-HT₁B, 5-HT₁D, 5-HT₁E and 5-HT₁F. Pharmacology notebook · Bockaert et al., receptor chapter

item.title: The Diuretic That Tried to Quiet Seizures — Neonatal Electrographic-Only Seizures, Developmental NKCC1/KCC2 Chloride Shift (Rivera/Dzhala), Bumetanide NKCC1 Cryo-EM (PDB 9C0H) & NEMO/Soul Trials
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 84: Neonatal Electrographic-Only Seizures, Developmental NKCC1/KCC2 Chloride Shift (Rivera/Dzhala), Bumetanide NKCC1 Cryo-EM (PDB 9C0H) & NEMO/Soul Trials. A newborn’s arm stops jerking. The scalp electrodes keep recording seizures. The Critical Care Clinician follows the discharges through cooling and rewarming. The Molecular Pharmacologist traces bumetanide from an edema patent to a chloride cotransporter. The case, measurements and dialogue are fictional. The notebook anchor is Criss Hartzell’s 2010 “Chloride Channels: An Historical Perspective.” Pharmacology notebook · Hartzell chapter

item.title: The Glucose That Fell Again — Azole-Gliclazide CYP2C9 Interaction, SUR1/KATP Beta-Cell Closure, Recurrent Dextrose Rebound & Octreotide Suppression Trials
item.description: Pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic feedback in recurrent sulfonylurea hypoglycemia: Gunaratne et al.'s (2018) nocturnal rebound drop from 106 to 25 mg/dL after voriconazole-to-fluconazole CYP2C9 inhibition with gliclazide, Aguilar-Bryan et al.'s (1995) cloning of beta-cell SUR1 gating KATP depolarization, Boyle et al.'s (1993) 8-volunteer crossover comparing dextrose alone, diazoxide, and octreotide, and Fasano et al.'s (2008) double-blind emergency-department octreotide RCT.

item.title: The Odor They Learned to Detect — Unilateral Nostril Androstenone Induction (Mainland 2002), Human OR7D4 Genetic Polymorphisms (Keller 2007) & Olfactory Training
item.description: Peripheral vs. central plasticity in human olfaction: Mainland et al.'s (2002) single-nostril exposure experiment showing contralateral transfer of acquired androstenone sensitivity, Keller et al.'s (2007) and Lunde et al.'s (2012) OR7D4 RT/WM receptor variants governing odor intensity and valence in pork taint, and Gillmeister et al.'s (2025) olfactory perceptual training.

item.title: The Metal the Hair Remembered — Familial Thallium Poisoning Blood/Urine vs. Postmortem Hair & Single-Strand LA-ICP-MS Longitudinal Profiling
item.description: Forensic toxicology of thallium across biological matrices: Di Candia et al.'s (2020) family poisoning investigation contrasting antemortem blood/urine clearance with postmortem keratin incorporation, Luo et al.'s (2017) single-hair laser ablation ICP-MS validation, and Matsukawa & Heitland longitudinal profiling limits.

item.title: The pH That Looked Normal — Salicylate Mixed Alkalosis-Acidosis Pseudo-Normal Venous pH, Non-Ionized Brain Partitioning (Kang 1990), Mitochondrial Uncoupling & Retained Bezoars
item.description: Acid-base physics and cellular bioenergetics in salicylate poisoning: Fernando et al.'s (2017) pseudo-normal venous pH masking simultaneous medullary respiratory alkalosis and high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, Kang et al.'s (1990) radiotracer proof that slight systemic acidemia dramatically increases unionized CNS salicylate entry, Smith et al.'s (2016) protonophoric mitochondrial uncoupling, and Parker-Cote et al.'s (2022) delayed rebound from retained gastric tablets.

item.title: When Maltose Read as Glucose — Icodextrin Peritoneal Dialysis Metabolites, GDH-PQQ Test-Strip Cross-Reactivity vs. Core-Lab Hexokinase & Occult Neuroglycopenia
item.description: Drug-assay cross-reactivity between peritoneal dialysis polymers and bedside point-of-care glucometers: Riley et al.'s (2003) icodextrin case where systemic alpha-amylase generated maltose/maltotriose that read as severe hyperglycemia on GDH-PQQ strips while true laboratory hexokinase glucose was critically low, Olszowska et al.'s (2019) metabolite kinetics, Cho et al.'s (2016) strip-enzyme interference bench testing, and Frias et al.'s (2010) FDA adverse-event series.

item.title: The Drug That Redirected Another — Azathioprine + Allopurinol Xanthine-Oxidase Blockade, 6-TGN Pancytopenia vs. 6-MMP Hepatotoxicity & Deliberate Low-Dose Co-Therapy
item.description: Metabolic pathway redirection in thiopurine pharmacology: Feinman et al.'s (2020) heart-transplant pancytopenia after unadjusted allopurinol addition blocked xanthine oxidase and flooded 6-thioguanine nucleotides (6-TGN), Blaker et al.'s (2013) thioxanthine-mediated TPMT inhibition in red cells, Aizawa et al.'s (2025) metabolite profiling, and Kiszka-Kanowitz et al.'s (2022) randomized trial harnessing low-dose thiopurine + allopurinol in ulcerative colitis.

item.title: The Antibiotic the Lung Turned Off — Daptomycin Sequestration by Pulmonary Surfactant Phosphatidylglycerol, Ca2+-Membrane Biophysics, Septic Emboli vs. Bronchial Pneumonia
item.description: Compartment-specific biophysical inactivation of lipopeptide antibiotics: Zainah et al.'s (2013) MRSA endocarditis case with septic pulmonary emboli, Machhua et al.'s (2025) structural chemistry of Ca2+-dependent daptomycin complexation with phosphatidylglycerol, Silverman/Schwameis surfactant time-kill inhibition in alveolar lining fluid, and Pertel et al.'s (2008) randomized FOCUS community-acquired pneumonia failure.

item.title: The Rhythm That Changed Its Shape — Flecainide 1:1 Atrial Flutter & Use-Dependent QRS Widening, Cardiac Nav1.5 Pore Block (Jiang 2020) & The CAST Surrogate-Endpoint Paradox
item.description: Ion-channel kinetics and clinical trial epistemology in Class IC antiarrhythmic therapy: Dardas et al.'s (2021/2022) flecainide atrial flutter 1:1 AV conduction with wide-complex tachycardia, Jiang et al.'s (2020 Cell) cryo-EM structure of cardiac Nav1.5 central-cavity flecainide binding, Ranger et al.'s (1989) exercise-amplified use-dependent QRS prolongation from slow unbinding, and the 1989 CAST mortality reversal.

item.title: The Burn That Came Before Relief — TRPV1 Cloning (Caterina 1997), Reversible Epidermal PGP 9.5 Nerve-Fiber Defunctionalization & 8% Capsaicin Patch Neuropathic Pain Trials
item.description: From nociceptor channel cloning to reversible peripheral nerve-ending remodeling: Caterina et al.'s (1997) expression cloning of the heat- and capsaicin-gated cation channel TRPV1, Kennedy et al.'s (2010) serial skin-punch biopsies quantifying ~80% reversible PGP 9.5 epidermal nerve-fiber loss and 24-week regeneration after a 60-minute 8% capsaicin patch, and contrasting Backonja (2008, low-dose active control in PHN) vs. Bischoff (2014, inert placebo in post-herniorrhaphy pain) RCT outcomes.

item.title: The Heart Block and the Falling Glucose — Verapamil Overdose AV Dissociation & Metabolic Shock, High-Dose Insulin Euglycemic Therapy (Kline 1993; Yuan 1999) & Poison-Center Evidence
item.description: Cardiovascular-metabolic coupling in severe L-type calcium-channel blocker poisoning: Malakian et al.'s (2026) verapamil dysrhythmia and hypoinsulinemic hyperglycemia trajectory, Kline et al.'s (1993) controlled canine survival comparison of insulin-dextrose vs. calcium, epinephrine, and glucagon, Yuan et al.'s (1999) early human high-dose insulin euglycemic case series, and Cole et al.'s (2018) 199-patient poison-center chart review of hypoglycemia and hypokalemia risks.

item.title: The Drug That Quieted the First Wave — Ondansetron & Cisplatin Emesis, 5-HT3A Cryo-EM (PDB 6W1M), Acute 5-HT3 vs. Delayed Substance P/NK1 Phase, hERG QTc Risk & CYP2D6 CPIC
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of ondansetron and biphasic chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting: Cubeddu & Marty's 1990 cisplatin trials, 2.8 Å cryo-EM structure of 5-HT3A bound to ondansetron (PDB 6W1M), why acute (0–24h) peripheral 5-HT3 vagal signaling gives way to delayed (24–120h) central NK1/Substance P signaling, hERG K+ channel blockade and FDA IV dose caps, and CPIC CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolizer guidance.

item.title: The Venom That Took the Spinal Route — Intrathecal Ziconotide (ω-Conotoxin MVIIA), Olivera's Conus magus Discovery, Human CaV2.2 Cryo-EM Pore Plug (PDB 7MIX) & Slow Titration
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of intrathecal ziconotide (PRIALT / omega-conotoxin MVIIA): Olivera's discovery of Conus magus peptide toxins, Nieng Yan's 3.1 Å cryo-EM structure of human CaV2.2 plugged by ziconotide (PDB 7MIX), why systemic IV delivery causes orthostatic hypotension via sympathetic CaV2.2 block while intrathecal delivery targets dorsal horn lamina I/II synapses without tolerance or respiratory depression, and Staats (2004) vs. Rauck (2006) titration kinetics.

item.title: The Amino Acid at the Brain's Gate — Six-Competitor Plasma Tryptophan Ratio, Human LAT1 Cryo-EM (8J8M/8XPU), TPH2 & PET Tracer Assumptions, Delgado's Remission Relapse Trials (14/21; 8/15 vs. 1/15) & Breakfast Limits
item.description: From plasma amino-acid competition at blood-brain barrier LAT1–CD98hc (PDB 8J8M L-Trp & 8XPU JPH203) to acute tryptophan depletion trials: UHPLC-MS/MS separation of isobaric Leu/Ile, recombinant TPH2 kinetics vs. alpha-[11C]methyl-L-Trp PET assumptions, Delgado's remitted depression crossover (14/21) and SSRI vs. desipramine responder split (8/15 vs. 1/15), and why Wurtman's breakfast study measured plasma ratios rather than mood.

item.title: The Gluten Fragment That Changed Its Charge — Celiac TG2 Cys277 Gln→Glu Deamidation, HLA-DQ2.5 Lysβ71 Pocket (1S9V), Irreversible ZED1227 Active-Site Trapping & Gluten-Challenge Biopsy Trials
item.description: Atomic pathogenesis and covalent enzyme inhibition in celiac disease: tissue transglutaminase 2 (TG2) Cys277 thioester deamidation of gliadin glutamine into negatively charged glutamate, HLA-DQ2.5 positively charged P4/P6/P7 pocket anchoring via Lysβ71 (PDB 1S9V), tTG-IgA vs. total IgA and Marsh/villus-height-to-crypt-depth morphometry, and Schuppan et al.'s (2021) NEJM ZED1227 trial.

item.title: The Bowel That Learned to Absorb Again — Short-Bowel High-Output Jejunostomy Secretory Losses, GLP-2R Cryo-EM & Teduglutide Ala2→Gly2 DPP-4 Shielding & STEPS Parenteral Weaning
item.description: Intestinal rehabilitation in short-bowel syndrome with end-jejunostomy: net secretory stoma sodium/water balance vs. renal sodium conservation, colonic salvage anatomy, human GLP-2–GLP-2R–Gs cryo-EM structure and teduglutide Ala2→Gly2 DPP-4 resistance, villus height/crypt depth trophic remodeling, and Jeppesen's STEPS randomized parenteral-support reduction trial.

item.title: The Calabar Bean & the Missing Signal — Physostigmine, Acetylcholinesterase Ser203 Carbamylation, Antimuscarinic Delirium & QRS Counterfactuals
item.description: From Efik esere ordeal records in Old Calabar and Thomas Richard Fraser's Edinburgh experiments to human acetylcholinesterase Ser203 carbamylation (4EY4/1GQR), false-positive urine TCA immunoassays, and ECG QRS gating in antimuscarinic delirium.

item.title: How a Blood Vessel Tells Itself to Relax — Furchgott & Zawadzki's 1980 Intact vs. Rubbed Rabbit Aorta, Rubanyi's Donor-Detector Perfusion, Palmer & Moncada's Ozone Chemiluminescence Nitric Oxide Proof & 15N-Arginine Tracing
item.description: How the vascular endothelium's relaxing signal was identified as nitric oxide: Furchgott & Zawadzki's (1980) discovery that removing the inner endothelial lining abolishes acetylcholine relaxation while preserving smooth-muscle contraction, Rubanyi et al.'s (1985) upstream donor/downstream denuded detector bioassay, Palmer, Ferrige & Moncada's (1987) chemiluminescent nitric oxide measurement alongside Ignarro's cGMP comparison, and 15N-arginine precursor tracing.

item.title: How Cells Tie Growth to Available Nutrients — Heitman & Hall's Yeast FPR1/TOR1/TOR2 Rapamycin Mutants, Sabatini & Brown's Mammalian mTOR Affinity Capture & Hara's Amino-Acid Withdrawal Gate
item.description: Discovery of the TOR nutrient-sensing pathway: Heitman, Movva & Hall (1991) genetic screen in Saccharomyces cerevisiae showing rapamycin requires FKBP12 (FPR1) to inhibit TOR1/TOR2, Sabatini et al. (1994) & Brown et al. (1994) biochemical capture of the ~289 kDa mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) only when rapamycin is bound to FKBP12, Barbet et al. (1996) starvation-like translation arrest, and Hara et al. (1998) amino-acid gating of insulin-stimulated p70S6K phosphorylation.

item.title: How a Cell Passes a Message Inside — Sutherland & Rall's Broken-Cell Liver Homogenate Fractionation, Heat-Stable Cyclic AMP Transfer & Walsh's cAMP-Dependent Protein Kinase
item.description: Discovery of the second-messenger principle: Rall, Sutherland & Berthet (1957) two-stage cell-free assay separating particulate membrane hormone response from soluble phosphorylase activation via a dialyzable, heat-stable factor, Sutherland & Rall (1958) chemical identification of cyclic 3',5'-AMP, and Walsh, Perkins & Krebs (1968) discovery of cAMP-dependent protein kinase (PKA).

item.title: The Mirror-Image Test for an Opioid Receptor — Goldstein's Stereospecificity, Pert & Snyder's [3H]Naloxone Levorphanol vs. Dextrorphan Assay & Enkephalin Discovery
item.description: Biochemical proof of brain opioid receptors: Goldstein et al. (1971) enantiomeric competition concept, Pert & Snyder (1973) [3H]naloxone vacuum-filtration assay showing stereospecific displacement by (-)-levorphanol but not (+)-dextrorphan, Hughes et al. (1975) discovery of endogenous pentapeptides Met- and Leu-enkephalin, and 1992 delta-receptor cloning.

item.title: The Signal the Poison Interrupted — Delayed Belladonna Atropine Rebound via LC-MS/MS, Scopolamine Hippocampal Theta Disruption & Physostigmine vs. Lorazepam in Antimuscarinic Delirium
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology investigation of central and peripheral muscarinic blockade: delayed gastrointestinal absorption and day-4 LC-MS/MS serum atropine rebound after belladonna ingestion (Hayashi et al. 2026), human intracranial EEG evidence of scopolamine disrupting hippocampal theta oscillations during memory encoding (Gedankien et al. 2023), and randomized trial evidence comparing physostigmine cholinesterase inhibition against lorazepam sedation in antimuscarinic delirium.

item.title: The Pump at the Brain — Blood-Brain Barrier P-Glycoprotein (ABCB1) Efflux, Loperamide vs. Fentanyl CNS Exclusion, Cryo-EM ATPase Cycle & Drug-Drug Interactions
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology deep dive into blood-brain barrier ABCB1 (P-glycoprotein) efflux: why potent mu-opioid agonists like loperamide act peripherally unless P-gp is overwhelmed or inhibited, inward-to-outward cryo-EM peristaltic extrusion, and clinical transporter inhibition.

item.title: The Muscle That Waited — Prolonged Post-Succinylcholine Neuromuscular Blockade, Zero Train-of-Four Twitches, Dibucaine Number 41 vs. Catalytic BChE Activity & BCHE Genotyping
item.description: Pharmacogenetics and clinical management of prolonged succinylcholine apnea (Hubbell et al. 2025): why a short-acting depolarizing neuromuscular blocker lasted 8 hours after hip surgery, peripheral nerve stimulator absence of twitches, distinguishing quantitative butyrylcholinesterase deficiency from qualitative atypical variants via the dibucaine inhibition number, and BCHE sequencing.

item.title: The Letter the First Test Missed — Compound Heterozygous DPYD Variants Missed by 4-SNP Panels (de Haar-Holleman 2024), Fluorouracil Catabolism Collapse & Uridine Triacetate Antidote Rescue
item.description: Pharmacogenomics and biochemical rescue of fluoropyrimidine toxicity: why targeted 4-variant DPYD genotyping misses rare in-trans compound heterozygotes (de Haar-Holleman et al. 2024), phenotypic DPD uracil breath/plasma assays (Coenen et al. 2019), 5-FU catabolic shunting into FUTP/FdUMP (Peters et al. 1988), and emergency antidote rescue with uridine triacetate (Jacob et al. 2022).

item.title: The Drug That Cut the Drug — Glucarpidase Methotrexate Rescue, DAMPA Immunoassay Cross-Reactivity vs. HPLC/LC-MS/MS (5.79 vs. 2.27 µmol/L at Hour 117, Gulley 2020), Ogawa Tissue Rebound & Organ Recovery
item.description: Enzymatic drug cleavage and analytical cross-reactivity after high-dose methotrexate rescue with glucarpidase (carboxypeptidase G2): Gulley et al.'s (2020) split specimen 74 hours post-glucarpidase reading 5.79 µmol/L by immunoassay vs. 2.27 µmol/L by HPLC due to DAMPA metabolite persistence beyond the nominal 48-hour VORAXAZE label window, Ogawa et al.'s (2024) 98.83% 20-minute plasma drop and tissue rebound, and Corbisier et al.'s (2024) multimodal pediatric liver/renal recovery.

item.title: The Blood That Would Not Turn Red — Acquired Methemoglobinemia (SpO2 86% vs. PaO2 85 mmHg), Multi-Wavelength Co-Oximetry, NADPH Reductase & G6PD Methylene Blue Hemolysis
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology deep dive into acquired methemoglobinemia and antidote mechanics: why dual-wavelength pulse oximetry locks near 85–86% despite high dissolved arterial PaO2, multi-wavelength co-oximetry separation of ferric (Fe3+) methemoglobin, how methylene blue uses NADPH methemoglobin reductase as an artificial electron shuttle, and why G6PD deficiency converts methylene blue into a trigger for acute Heinz-body hemolysis (Mathiyalagan et al. 2025; ProvayBlue US label).

item.title: The Number the Antidote Raised — Digoxin Immune Fab Redistribution vs. Immunoassay Interference, Ultrafiltration Free Digoxin (Jortani 1999), Renal Rebound Kinetics (Ujhelyi 1993) & Chronic Cardiogenic Shock
item.description: Separating true pharmacokinetic tissue redistribution from platform-dependent immunoassay interference after digoxin immune Fab: Smith et al. (1976) 12-fold total serum rise with undetectable free digoxin, Jortani et al. (1999) ultrafiltrate immunoassay bias across platforms, Ujhelyi et al. (1993) delayed free-digoxin rebound in renal dysfunction, and Gerritsma et al. (2025) chronic digoxin cardiogenic shock.

item.title: The Antibiotic at the Other Ribosome — Linezolid Hyperlactatemia, Mitoribosome COX-II vs. Nuclear Tom20/SDHA Translation, Paired PBMC Recovery & Duration Cohort Denominators
item.description: Translational pharmacology and mitochondrial toxicology of oxazolidinone antibiotics: linezolid-associated hyperlactatemia despite 98% arterial oxygen saturation (Chaudhri et al. 2024, 4.9->5.1->1.6 mmol/L), selective depletion of mitoribosome-encoded cytochrome c oxidase subunits vs. nuclear-encoded Tom20 and SDHA in human HL-60/THP-1 cells (Milosevic et al. 2018), paired patient PBMC recovery (Garrabou et al. 2007, COX-II protein 16% and enzyme activity 51% of controls with intact mtDNA/mRNA), and 40-patient cross-sectional duration cohorts (Martínez-Guitián et al. 2026).

item.title: The Drug That Changed With the Fever — Clozapine 1975 Finland Cluster & Kane 1988 Trial, Human H4–Gi Structure (PDB 8JXV), CYP1A2 Inflammation/Smoking Shift & AGP Binding
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 82: from the 1975 Finnish agranulocytosis cluster (Idänpään-Heikkilä et al.) and Kane et al.'s (1988) treatment-resistant schizophrenia trial (38/126 vs. 5/141) to ancillary human H4-Gi cryo-EM structure (PDB 8JXV), why acute pneumonia and abrupt smoking cessation elevate serum clozapine and the clozapine:norclozapine ratio via IL-6 CYP1A2 suppression and de-induction (Faber & Fuhr; Dickmann; Raaska), alpha-1-acid glycoprotein (AGP) unbound-fraction buffering, and the June 2025 FDA clozapine REMS removal.

item.title: The Channel That Quieted Insulin — Congenital Hyperinsulinism Critical Samples, Diazoxide KATP Opening, SUR1/Kir6.2 Comparator (PDB 7W4O), KCNJ11 Genetics & Pulmonary Hypertension
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 81: neonatal hypoketotic hypoglycemia critical-sample diagnostics (simultaneous glucose, insulin, C-peptide, beta-hydroxybutyrate, and free fatty acids; Ferrara et al.), repurposing antihypertensive benzothiadiazine diazoxide (Drash & Wolff 1964), beta-cell SUR1/Kir6.2 KATP opening and NN414 comparator structure (PDB 7W4O), dominant KCNJ11 p.Phe55Leu gating vs. recessive focal 11p15 loss, and echocardiographic surveillance for diazoxide-associated pulmonary hypertension (Herrera et al., 7/295).

item.title: The Drug That Emptied the Vesicle — Rauwolfia & Reserpine Discovery, Human VMAT2 Cytoplasm-Facing Complex (PDB 8JTC), Orthostatic ΔHR/ΔSBP & Prolonged Monoamine Depletion
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 80: from Vakil's (1949) Rauwolfia root reports and Müller, Schlittler & Bein's (1952) reserpine isolation to V-ATPase 2H+:1 amine stoichiometry (Knoth et al.), human VMAT2-reserpine cytoplasm-facing cryo-EM coordinates (Wu et al. PDB 8JTC, Tyr341/Tyr433; Pidathala et al. PDB 8T6A), why noncovalent transporter blockade produces prolonged vesicular monoamine depletion and blunted orthostatic heart-rate compensation, and bounded interpretation of Freis's (1954) depression case series.

item.title: The Walk That Became a Seizure — Dalfampridine (4-AP) in Demyelinated Axons, Kv1.2/Kv2.1 Architecture (PDB 2R9R), Timed-Walk Trial Denominators & Renal Seizure Risk
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 77: dalfampridine (4-aminopyridine) conduction rescue in diphtheria-toxin demyelinated rat spinal roots (Bostock, Sherratt & Sears 1978–1981), Kv1.2/Kv2.1 paddle-chimera selectivity filter coordinates (PDB 2R9R, Val371/Gly372), Goodman et al. (2009, 2010) Phase 3 timed 25-foot walk responder denominators (78/224 vs. 6/72; 51/119 vs. 11/118), extended-release vs. oral solution Cmax, and why renal impairment (CrCl <= 50 mL/min) precipitates acute seizures.

item.title: The Rhythm the Drug Could Break — Dofetilide (Tikosyn) Inpatient QT Gate, Human hERG Cryo-EM Cavity (PDB 5VA2), Reverse Use-Dependence, Renal OCT2/MATE1 & the DIAMOND Trials
item.description: Biophysics, structural biology, and clinical safety engineering of dofetilide (Tikosyn): Sanguinetti's IKr/hERG discovery, Wang & MacKinnon's human Kv11.1 cryo-EM structure (PDB 5VA2) and Tyr652/Phe656 drug-trapping cavity, reverse use-dependence at slow sinus rates after cardioversion, renal OCT2/MATE1 transport interactions, and the DIAMOND trials.

item.title: The Cocaine Signal That Stayed Behind — Cocaine-Associated Chest Pain, Serial hs-cTnI Trajectory, Human DAT-Cocaine Cryo-EM (PDB 9EO4), Benzoylecgonine/Cocaethylene LC-MS/MS & Lange Vasospasm
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology & Forensic Toxicology of cocaine: why urine immunoassays detect hydrolytic metabolite benzoylecgonine for days after parent cocaine (T1/2 ~1h) has cleared, Nielsen et al.'s (2024) 2.66 Å cryo-EM structure of human DAT bound to cocaine (PDB 9EO4), hepatic carboxylesterase transesterification with ethanol to form long-acting cocaethylene, serial hs-cTnI rule-in, and Lange et al.'s (1989, 1990) coronary catheterization proof of alpha-adrenergic vasospasm.

item.title: The Spasticity Drug the Kidney Kept — Oral Baclofen Coma in CKD, Bowery's GABAB Discovery, Human GABAB1-GABAB2 Cryo-EM (PDB 4MS4/7EB2), Triphasic EEG & EXTRIP Hemodialysis
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of baclofen neurotoxicity in renal impairment: Keberle's 1962 lipophilic GABA design and Bowery's 1980 GABAB receptor discovery, human GABAB1-GABAB2 heterodimer crystal/cryo-EM structures (PDB 4MS4, 7EB2), why 69–85% unchanged renal clearance causes rapid accumulation, triphasic/burst-suppression encephalopathy, and coma in CKD (Muanda et al. 2019), and EXTRIP guideline criteria for emergent hemodialysis.

item.title: The First Breath Caffeine Bought — Apnea of Prematurity, Aranda's 1977 Trial, Human A2A Receptor Cryo-EM/X-Ray (PDB 5MZP/5G53), CYP1A2 Ontogeny & CAP Trial Outcomes
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of caffeine citrate in apnea of prematurity: central vs. obstructive vs. mixed apnea traces, Aranda et al. (1977) and Murat et al. (1981) clinical trials, human A2A receptor crystal structures (PDB 5MZP, 5G53) showing competitive adenosine blockade, neonatal CYP1A2 ontogeny (~100-hour T1/2 vs. 4–6 hours in adults) and 2:1 salt-to-base dosing safety, and the 2,006-infant CAP trial through age 11 (Schmidt et al. 2006, 2007, 2017).

item.title: The Drug That Changed the Ward — Chlorpromazine from Rhône-Poulenc Patent & 1952 Psychiatric Wards (Laborit, Delay & Elkes) to Pause-Triggered Torsades, Human hERG Cryo-EM (5VA1), DRD2 Kinetics & Sulfoxide LC-MS/MS
item.description: Two ward records seventy years apart: chlorpromazine's transition from Rhône-Poulenc synthesis (US2645640A) and Laborit's 1952 surgical 'artificial hibernation' to Delay & Deniker's psychiatric cases, Elkes & Elkes's 1954 crossover, and the 1964 NIMH Collaborative Study, paired with a contemporary pause-triggered torsades workup (Fridericia QTc 531 ms), ligand-free human hERG cryo-EM (PDB 5VA1), oocyte vs. CHO IC50s (21.6 vs. 1.47 µM), and DRD2 residence kinetics.

item.title: The Fat Droplet That Wouldn't Let Go — PNPLA3 I148M Droplet Sequestration & ABHD5 Competition, Romeo's Dallas Heart Study Scan, MRI-PDFF vs. FIB-4 & AZD2693 Antisense FORTUNA Trial
item.description: Why knocking out Pnpla3 in mice did not cause fatty liver while human PNPLA3 I148M drives steatohepatitis: Romeo et al. (2008) 1H-MRS genetics, Ser47–Asp166 patatin dyad, ubiquitylation-resistant I148M accumulation on lipid droplets sequestering CGI-58/ABHD5 away from ATGL (Wang et al. 2019), and phase I/IIb GalNAc-ASO AZD2693 MRI-PDFF reductions vs. FORTUNA histologic fibrosis endpoints.

item.title: The First Calories Back — Refeeding Syndrome, Insulin-Driven Phosphate/Potassium Shifts, PDH E1 ThDP Geometry (1NI4) & Doig ICU Trial
item.description: From starvation to refeeding syndrome in the ICU: insulin-stimulated Na+/K+-ATPase potassium uptake and intracellular phosphate trapping, human pyruvate dehydrogenase E1 thiamine diphosphate (ThDP) active-site geometry (PDB 1NI4), whole-blood ThDP LC-MS/MS assays, diaphragmatic weakness in hypophosphatemia (Aubier 1985), and the Doig et al. (2015) caloric restriction trial.

item.title: Warfarin & the Three Clocks of Bleeding — Spoiled Sweet Clover, VKORC1 Asn80/Tyr139, Chiral S/R-Warfarin m/z 307→161, 4F-PCC vs. INR & Serial ICH CT
item.description: From spoiled sweet-clover hemorrhagic disease and Link's 1947 patent to human VKORC1 Asn80/Tyr139 crystal contacts, chiral LC-MS/MS separation of S- and R-warfarin (sharing m/z 307->161), and separating the three clinical clocks of drug clearance, factor replacement (4F-PCC vs. plasma), and intracerebral hematoma expansion.

item.title: The Blue Dye & the Oxygen Number — Methylene Blue, Acquired Methemoglobinemia, Two-Wavelength SpO2 vs. Co-Oximetry & G6PD Limits
item.description: How an industrial phenothiazine dye became the antidote for acquired methemoglobinemia—and why both ferric methemoglobin (660/940 nm) and intravenous methylene blue itself spoof two-wavelength pulse oximeters toward an ~85% plateau while multiwavelength co-oximetry separates fractional species.

item.title: Why a Pulse Oximeter Needs a Pulse — Millikan & Wood's Bloodless Ear Zero, Takuo Aoyagi's 1974 Pulsatile AC/DC Ratio, Dyshemoglobin 85% Artifacts & Skin-Pigment Bias
item.description: Optical physics and physiological limitations of pulse oximetry: Millikan (1942) and Wood & Geraci's (1949) pneumatic bloodless-ear zeroing, Takuo Aoyagi's (1974) breakthrough using pulsatile arterial AC/DC absorbance ratios at two wavelengths, two-wavelength degrees-of-freedom failure in carboxyhemoglobinemia and methemoglobinemia, and melanin/low-saturation occult hypoxemia bias (Bickler et al. 2005; Sjoding et al. 2020).

item.title: How an Electrode Learned to Measure Glucose — Clark & Lyons's 1962 Enzyme Membrane Electrode, Updike & Hicks's 1967 Dual-Cathode Differential Sensor & Basu's 2013 Interstitial Lag
item.description: Electrochemical and physiological foundations of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM): Clark & Lyons's (1962) enzyme-membrane electrode concept, Updike & Hicks's (1967) dual-cathode active-vs-inactivated polyacrylamide 'enzyme electrode' canceling ambient oxygen drift, subcutaneous interstitial fluid sensing and electroactive drug interference, and Basu et al.'s (2013) human tracer microdialysis proof of physiological capillary-to-interstitial glucose lag.

item.title: Gill Lamellae, Trunk Kidneys, Exhaust Dust, and Brainstems — Teleost Gill Wet Mounts & Gas Bubble Disease (V053), Aquatic Kidney Culture, 37°C Traps & FDA VFDs (V054), Lab Rodent Exhaust Air Dust PCR (V055) & Wildlife Rabies DFA & CDC LN34 RT-qPCR (V056)
item.description: One Medicine Capstone synthesis of teleost wet mounts (V053), fish bacteriology (V054), lab rodent surveillance (V055), and wildlife rabies testing (V056): 15m gill autolysis clock, buffered MS-222, Gyrodactylus vs. Dactylogyrus, and Gas Bubble Disease; Posterior Trunk Kidney culture, 15-28C thermal/TYES media, CLSI VET03/04, and FDA VFD law; IVC Exhaust Air Dust qPCR, NSG serology traps, binomial n=299 math, and LCMV biologics PCR; and bilateral Brainstem+Cerebellum DFA, CDC LN34 decomposed-brain rescue, cryptic bedroom bats, and FAVN titers.

item.title: The Number After the Blood Was Cleared — Pre-Dialysis Lithium Rebound, 7Li Brain MRS Half-Life, Spent-Tank Dialysate Recovery & EXTRIP Cohort Predictions
item.description: Multi-compartment pharmacokinetics and clinical toxicology of lithium clearance: pre-dialysis serum rebound during IV hydration in chronic toxicity with nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (Kobylianskii et al. 2021, 1.50->0.40->1.30 mmol/L), human 7Li brain magnetic resonance spectroscopy vs. serum half-lives (Plenge et al. 1994), direct mass recovery of 250 mg lithium in collected spent dialysate vs. serum percentage reduction (Schmidt et al. 2014), and retrospective evaluation of EXTRIP dialysis criteria across 361 poisonings (Buckley et al. 2020).

item.title: The Level That Rose After the Last Pill — Delayed Enteric & Modified-Release Absorption, Pharmacobezoars, Auto-Inhibition & Rising Post-Admission Drug Levels
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology investigation of rising post-ingestion drug concentrations in hospitalized patients: modified-release formulation kinetics, pyloric spasm and ileus, pharmacobezoar formation, and why a single triage drug level misses late peak toxicity.

item.title: What the Hair Could Tell Us — Early Iron Age Tunnug 1 Cannabis Burial, Hair-Shaft CBN LC-HRMS/MS vs. Environmental Transfer, Human CB1-Gi1 Cryo-EM (PDB 9ERX) & Hallstatt Radiocarbon
item.description: Archaeotoxicology and receptor pharmacology of ancient cannabis at Tunnug 1 (Tuva, Early Iron Age): LC-HRMS/MS detection of cannabinol (CBN) in a preserved human hair braid alongside 965 botanical cannabis seeds, Hallstatt Plateau 14C calibration, human CB1-Gi1 cryo-EM structure (PDB 9ERX), forensic hair-testing boundaries between smoke/handling transfer and metabolic THC-COOH incorporation (Moosmann et al. 2015), and comparative Eurasian archaeobotany.

item.title: The Aspirin That Changed the Breathing — Hoffmann's Acetylsalicylic Acid, Vane's Prostaglandin Blockade & Human COX-2 Ser530 Acetylation (5F19 vs. 5F1A), Mitochondrial Uncoupling, Chloride Electrode Artifacts & EXTRIP Dialysis
item.description: Covalent enzyme acetylation meets clinical toxicology: Hoffmann's 1900 aspirin patent, Vane and Smith & Willis's 1971 prostaglandin inhibition, Roth's irreversible platelet COX acetylation, and Lucido's human COX-2 crystal structures (acetylated Ser530 in PDB 5F19 vs. salicylate-bound 5F1A), paired with a serial salicylate poisoning timeline showing mixed respiratory alkalosis and high-anion-gap acidosis, salicylate-induced chloride ISE pseudohyperchloremia, mitochondrial protonophoric uncoupling, pH-dependent nonionized CNS entry, and EXTRIP hemodialysis criteria.

item.title: Lithium and the Level That Came Back — Cade & Schou, Lithium-Heparin Tube Artifacts, GSK-3β Mg2+ Competition, ENaC Nephrogenic DI & Post-Dialysis Rebound
item.description: Clinical and molecular dissection of lithium toxicity: lithium-heparin green-top collection tube false elevations (Wills et al.), GSK-3β and IMPase Mg2+ competition (PDB 1PYX, 2BJI), collecting-duct ENaC entry (PDB 6BQN) and AQP2 downregulation, and EXTRIP hemodialysis rebound kinetics.

item.title: Foxglove, Digoxin & the Number That Rose After Rescue — Withering's Dropsy, Na+/K+-ATPase 4RET, DigiFab Immunoassay Interference & Free vs. Total LC-MS/MS
item.description: From William Withering's 1785 dropsy cases to the 4 A porcine Na+/K+-ATPase crystal structure (4RET), UHPLC-MS/MS MRM transitions, and why ovine DigiFab rescue causes total serum digoxin immunoassays to surge twelvefold while free pharmacologically active digoxin plummets.

item.title: The Number After the Sting — Postmortem Tryptase Site Divergence (8,955 Antemortem vs. <5,000 Central vs. 319 Peripheral ng/mL), Systemic Mastocytosis Baselines & Anaphylaxis Thresholds
item.description: Forensic pathology and clinical toxicology of fatal insect-sting anaphylaxis: dramatic divergence between antemortem catheter blood (8,955 ng/mL), postmortem central blood (<5,000 ng/mL), and postmortem peripheral femoral blood (319 ng/mL), systemic mastocytosis baseline tryptase elevation, and why isolated postmortem cutoffs fail without anatomic sampling discipline.

item.title: The Lunch That Looked Like an Allergy — Scombroid Histamine Fish Poisoning, Paris Yellowfin Tuna Outbreak (40 Cases, 39/79 Attack Rate), Heat-Stable Histidine Decarboxylation & Supply-Chain Forensics
item.description: Outbreak epidemiology and food toxicology of scombroid histamine fish poisoning: Velut et al.'s (2019) Paris military-canteen yellowfin tuna outbreak (40 cases, 39/79 tuna diners vs. 31-case/63-control questionnaire), bacterial histidine decarboxylation into heat-stable histamine mimicking IgE anaphylaxis, CDC 2006 Louisiana/Tennessee tuna traceback contrasts, and FDA CPG 540.525 surveillance rules.

item.title: The Lactate That Wasn't There — Ethylene Glycol Poisoning, Point-of-Care Glycolate Oxidase Cross-Reactivity & True Lab Lactate
item.description: Behind the Curtain forensic & clinical toxicology analysis of ethylene glycol poisoning: why blood-gas point-of-care L-lactate oxidase electrodes misread glycolate as massive hyperlactatemia while core-lab assays reveal the true lactate gap (Hauvik et al. 2018).

item.title: What the Bottle Could Not Tell — Postmortem Toxicology Redistribution, Pill-Bottle Scene Priors vs. Femoral Blood Quantification & Tolerance Boundaries

item.title: The Channel That Wouldn't Let Calcium Through — Extended-Release Verapamil Overdose, Fleckenstein's Calcium Antagonism, Rabbit CaV1.1 Cryo-EM (6JPA), Beta-Cell Hyperglycemia & High-Dose Insulin Therapy
item.description: From Albrecht Fleckenstein's discovery of calcium antagonism to critical-care toxicology: rabbit CaV1.1 cryo-EM structure bound to (S)-verapamil in two central-cavity poses (PDB 6JPA), AV-nodal conduction block, pancreatic beta-cell L-type channel blockade producing diagnostic hyperglycemia, stereoselective CYP3A4 clearance, high-dose insulin euglycemia therapy, and EXTRIP non-dialyzability.

item.title: The Sedative the Screen Missed — GABAA alpha1-beta2-gamma2 Cryo-EM Allosteric Binding (6X3X/6X3U), Diazepam CYP2C19/3A4 vs. Lorazepam Direct UGT2B15 Glucuronidation & Why Urine Immunoassays Miss Lorazepam-Glucuronide
item.description: Receptor allostery, metabolic routing, and toxicology screen blind spots: cryo-EM structures of human alpha1-beta2-gamma2 GABAA receptors bound to diazepam (PDB 6X3X) and flumazenil (PDB 6X3U), Sternbach's benzodiazepine chemistry, diazepam CYP oxidation vs. lorazepam direct C3-OH glucuronidation, and why unhydrolyzed urine benzodiazepine immunoassays miss lorazepam-glucuronide without beta-glucuronidase hydrolysis and LC-MS/MS.

item.title: The Dose That Bought Another Hour — Parkinson's Levodopa Wearing-Off Diaries, Catechol-O-Methyltransferase (COMT) Mg2+ Coordination (PDB 7XGI), Opicapone Erythrocyte Kinetics, BIPARK-I & Tolcapone Hepatotoxicity
item.description: From Parkinson's wearing-off diaries to peripheral COMT inhibition: separating seated motor OFF time from orthostatic hypotension, competing AADC and COMT metabolic pathways, rat soluble COMT crystal structure bound to opicapone and Mg2+ (PDB 7XGI), plasma LC-MS/MS vs. sustained erythrocyte COMT inhibition kinetics, BIPARK-I/II trial endpoints, and tolcapone vs. opicapone hepatic safety.

item.title: The Dose the Liver Had to Finish — Clopidogrel Thienopyridine Prodrug Bioactivation, CYP2C19 Loss-of-Function Alleles, Rapid GMEX Genotyping & the CHANCE-2 Trial

item.title: Half-Lives, Pancreatic Epitopes, and Portal Shunts — Human Therapeutic Drug Monitoring, Vancomycin AUC24 & Winter-Tozer/DigiFab Traps (H056), Canine/Feline Monoclonal Spec cPL/fPL & Triaditis (V025) & Dynamic Paired Bile Acids, Maltese Artifacts & PSS vs. MVD (V026)
